source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #250 (branch fix/154-debug-stack-overflow at commit b8eb7bf4ce5cec847431a4bef04bfeefceddbb6b, the merge of the PR head e450be821b6d628fc91f7ae9f81977e1ce8caae7 with main 2b650a24baab9d240cdb05868415eea4e3cf85b2; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45049989641 and 45050025929 against the branch and pull-request run 45047955830, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #250 (#154, debug-profile stack overflows). The PR's only release-relevant change splits the continuation computation of special_function_return in crates/telomere/src/runtime/vm/control.rs into an #[inline(never)] helper (prepare_function_return) so the tail dispatch stays a sibling call in non-LTO builds; the telomere library is linked into every embedder configuration, so the resulting code-layout shift moves gated sizes slightly in both directions (release stripped .text -16 B in core, component, wasi, core-nosimd and wasi-threads; release core-jit +80 B stripped file / +48 B stripped .text; release-size core and core-nosimd -80 B / -48 B, component, wasi and core-jit +16..+32 B, wasi-threads +16 B stripped file; 12 of 28 gated series unchanged, largest absolute delta 80 B). Attribution was cross-checked by measuring the PR head alone (e450be821b6d628fc91f7ae9f81977e1ce8caae7, before main was merged in) against the original 6c43ca67ae7c975fa52641b2eeaca3ca26f8f4ca baseline: workflow_dispatch runs 45049436565 and 45049445764 showed the same delta pattern. The PR's other build change, [profile.dev.package.telomere] in Cargo.toml, applies to dev profiles only and cannot affect these release measurements. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, 'Size regression gate (#164)'.
